items.title: Boardroom MCP - Multi-advisor governance engine for AI agents
items.raw_excerpt:
Hey HN, I noticed a recurring issue when building autonomous agents: they're great at execution but terrible at nuanced judgment. When faced with ambiguity, they just hallucinate the most statistically probable path without considering second-order effects. Instead of trying to fix this with massive system prompts, I built an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that offloads decisions to a multi-advisor "boardroom." How it works:
1. Agent encounters a decision -> calls the `analyze()` MCP tool.
2. Server routes the query to relevant advisors (from 38 domains, 450+ profiles).
3. Advisors debate. This is the core mechanic: if advisors agree too quickly, the system flags it. Tension is mandatory.

items.raw_excerpt: A few days ago, I built AI Council — a tool where multiple AI personas debate a question (CFO, Lawyer, Contrarian, Chairman, etc.). By Day 4, it evolved into AI Studio. Key changes: • 5-page navigation with auth-aware routing • 40+ categorized personas • 18 AI agent templates • Extracted Council component (2-column layout, inline editing, stage cards) • Searchable PersonaPicker and ModelPicker • Soft vs hard auth-gate patterns • Voice chat modal • MCP integration panel The bigger additions: You can now chat with personas directly via WhatsApp. There’s also an Assistant Mode with memory support, designed to act as a persistent personal AI layer rather than a stateless chat session. The system runs on Sarvam AI. Live demo: https://council.gameinghub.com/ Source: https://github.com/prijak/Ai-

items.title: Moltgram, a social network where only AI agents can post
items.raw_excerpt:
I built this because I wanted to see what a social feed looks like when humans are completely locked out of posting. Think Instagram but every photo and caption has to come from an AI agent. Humans can only browse.
The easiest way to try it is with OpenClaw or MCP. The skill is on ClawHub and on moltgram-api-production.up.railway.app/skill.md. Once installed, your agent can register itself, generate an AI image and post, all in one conversation.
The feed is public with no login needed. Every post requires an AI generated image, agents pick from several models including FLUX and Google Imagen 4.

items.title: Which web frameworks are most token-efficient for AI agents?

excerpt_i18n.en: I benchmarked 19 web frameworks on how efficiently an AI coding agent can build and extend the same app. Minimal frameworks cost up to 2.9x fewer tokens than full-featured ones.
